title: Define engine-neutral authored operations and revisions
description:
## Outcome
Define engine-neutral authored operations and revisions. The behaviour is available through the CalcDoc production path described below, with the named acceptance cases passing.

## Context
Implements §§2, 3, 7 of DNA_CALC_REIMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, within Bootstrap checkpoint — independent lanes, CI and evidence safety. Own only CalcDoc files for this task; consume prerequisite APIs rather than editing another library. Production route: calc_doc::open / prepare_edit / prepare_save / write; inspect the emitted package independently.

## Do
In calc-doc-model define AuthoredRevision, immutable model roots, WorkbookOp batches, structural-edit descriptors, CellInput and document-only metadata. The operation schema contains no engine/session types and never serializes computed cache as authored input. Generate per-capability operation codecs.
Add the named acceptance tests to this package's acceptance suite and register their exact names in its local acceptance manifest. Keep imported-source blob IDs and any changed semantic witnesses in the migration record. All proposed commands become real repository commands through infra-m0.3; a zero-test run is a failure.

## Port from
fresh; design these neutral types from this plan. OxDoc model names are not copied into the bootstrap contract.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo test -p calc-doc --test acceptance cdoc_m0_1 -- --nocapture
cargo xtask accept --id cdoc-m0.1 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id cdoc-m0.1 --platform linux --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id cdoc-m0.1 --platform wasm --require-all
```
- `cdoc_m0_1__op_roundtrip`: Every initially admitted operation round-trips through the versioned wire codec.
- `cdoc_m0_1__no_engine_dependency`: The model package compiles without CalcEngine, CalcFml or CalcHost and a cached value cannot be decoded as an authored formula replacement.
The acceptance runner must verify every named case actually executed and retain the machine-readable receipt. Assertions compare observable outputs, operation effects or independently instrumented calls, not a success flag assigned by the implementation itself.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux native tests, plus actual wasm browser execution in Chromium and Firefox. Run the same semantic fixtures on every target; platform adapters also have their native integration tests.

## Out of scope
Other command/function families and performance tuning. Do not add a second evaluator, a tree reference language, platform-specific code to portable libraries, or a hidden fallback. Any missing prerequisite requires an explicit dependent bead, not a local substitute.
notes:
Provisional plan ID: cdoc-m0.1. Native export preserves this ID; acceptance command IDs and test names use the same stable plan identity.

Sharpened at claim (2026-10-15):
- Package and route. The types and the operation codec live in crates/calc-doc-model, which CalcEngine may depend on (never on calc-doc, the package codec). calc-doc-model depends on calc-value (plan 2.1, MODEL to VALUE). calc-doc depends on calc-doc-model and re-exports it, and the two named cases live in crates/calc-doc/tests/acceptance.rs, registered in crates/calc-doc/acceptance.json for windows, linux and wasm. The cases reach the types only through calc-doc's re-export. calc_doc::open, prepare_edit, prepare_save and write arrive with the cdoc-m1 beads; this bead adds none of them, and no stand-in.
- Port: fresh. OxDoc is not read for this bead, and none of its model names (nor its OxCalc* symbols) enter CalcDoc. No migration record.
- Initially admitted operations. WorkbookOp has exactly these variants:
  - SetCell { at: CellKey, input: CellInput }.
  - Clear { area: GridArea }, which clears authored contents.
  - EditAxis(AxisEdit): insert or delete rows or columns on one sheet, with 1-based checked positions, a count of at least 1, within the grid.
  - EditSheet(SheetEdit): insert, rename, move, remove, and set visibility.
  AxisEdit and SheetEdit are the structural-edit descriptors. The other families in plan 2.2's sketch (Fill, MoveCells, EditName, EditTable, EditRule, EditStyle, EditObject, EditSettings, EditSkinLayout) are added by the beads that implement them, and the report names, from docs/plan/BEAD_DETAILS.md, the bead that owns each.
- CellInput:
  - Number: a finite binary64, keeping -0.0 and subnormals.
  - Text: ExcelText, keeping its code units, a dangling surrogate included.
  - Logical.
  - Error: WorksheetErrorCode.
  - Formula: the formula's source text and nothing else, so no cached value and no parse result.
  No variant holds a calculated value.
- Document-only metadata: facts the engine never reads, starting with sheet visibility (visible, hidden, very hidden), which a SheetEdit sets.
- AuthoredRevision is a u64 newtype with a checked next. OpBatch { base: AuthoredRevision, operations } holds WorkbookOps only. This deviates from plan 2.2's sketch on purpose: that sketch's OpBatch also carried a CommandSource and SessionOps. SessionOps are session types, which this Do excludes. The command source and undo grouping belong to CalcHost's journal (chost-m1 and chost-m2.2).
- Model root: an immutable, Arc-shared ModelRoot holding its AuthoredRevision and the sheets in order, each with its SheetId, SheetKey, name and visibility. It has no cell storage yet; the cdoc-m1 beads and ceng-m1.1 add authored pages.
- IDs on the wire. calc-value's IDs are allocator-scoped and have no raw constructor (cfunc-m0.1), and a retained journal must replay in a later session (chost-m2.2, chost-m6.4). So the wire never carries a SheetId. Each sheet has a document-stable SheetKey: a u32, unique and never reused within one document (the xlsx sheetId attribute plays that role). The model root maps SheetKey to SheetId; the wire carries SheetKeys, and decoding resolves them through the receiving model root. An unknown key is a typed decode error. A SheetEdit insert carries the new sheet's SheetKey; its SheetId is issued when the edit is applied, which is the cdoc-m1 beads' work.
- Wire codec:
  - One codec per capability (cells, axes, sheets), each generated from that capability's declaration.
  - An envelope names the capability and its version.
  - An unknown capability, a newer version, an unknown field or a non-finite number is a typed refusal, never a silent drop.
  - serde =1.0.229 (with derive) and serde_json =1.0.154 may be normal dependencies of calc-doc-model; both are already in Cargo.lock and license-reviewed through xtask.
  - Numbers travel as their binary64 bits in hex (plan 10.1: no decimal round trip). Text travels as UTF-16 code units, so a dangling surrogate survives.
- Case cdoc_m0_1__op_roundtrip covers every admitted variant, every CellInput kind, and every AxisEdit and SheetEdit kind:
  - Encoding and then decoding through a model root gives the original.
  - Committed golden fixture files decode to the expected operations and re-encode byte for byte. The fixtures live in crates/calc-doc/tests/fixtures/ and are read with include_bytes!, so the browsers read the same bytes.
  - The edge values are -0.0, the smallest subnormal, the largest finite, a 32,767-unit text, a text ending in a high surrogate, every WorksheetErrorCode, and XFD1048576.
  - A newer version or an unknown capability is refused.
- Case cdoc_m0_1__no_engine_dependency has three parts:
  - The case computes calc-doc-model's dependency closure from the committed Cargo.lock bytes, read through include_str! so the browsers run the same check, and finds none of calc-engine, calc-fml, calc-host or calc-doc. Cargo.lock lists every target's and feature's edges, so this over-approximates the real closure.
  - A wire batch whose formula input also carries a cached value is refused, and so is a message holding a calculated value.
  - A value literal never decodes as a formula.
- wasm: AGENTS.md's browser-test convention (wasm-bindgen =0.2.117 and wasm-bindgen-test =0.3.67 as wasm32-only dev-dependencies) applies to calc-doc and to calc-doc-model if it has unit tests.
- seams.json of calc-doc-model and calc-doc: every pub enum variant and trait is listed, with a non-test caller that its named case executes. Entries whose callers are all inside calc-doc-model are counted, and the orchestrator files their follow-up, as dc-0oyu does for calc-value.
- Adversarial class (M0 exit bead): refuters and judge at xhigh effort, and a mutation probe after the build commit, before the push.
Rulings after rounds 1 and 2 (2026-10-15):
- The golden fixtures are checked on their own. The case reads them as plain JSON and compares every operation's members with literal values written in the test. A claim that they came from a separate writer is not kept, because the writer was not kept.
- Limits stated on the items they concern rather than checked here, each with its owner in the tracker:
  - a batch acting on a sheet it inserts earlier, or on one it removed earlier: cdoc-m4.3;
  - never reusing a removed sheet's key: cdoc-m4.3;
  - comparing the batch base with the root's revision: chost-m1.1;
  - wire integers above 2^53 for browser-side readers: chost-m1.1;
  - formula length: cdoc-m1.2;
  - Excel's sheet-name rules: dc-85qk.
- Follow-ups filed: dc-kzkj (calc-doc-model seams entries with callers outside calc-doc-model; blocks dc-pz3u), dc-7qtj (a calc-doc-model layering rule in architecture.json) and dc-85qk. The beads that own the other WorkbookOp families (cdoc-m4.2, cdoc-m3.1, cdoc-m3.2, cdoc-m5.2, cdoc-m5.3, cdoc-m3.6, cdoc-m6.1, cdoc-m3.5, cdoc-m6.3, cdoc-m6.5 and cdoc-m2.1) each carry a note.
- The production route calc_doc::open, prepare_edit, prepare_save and write is absent by the claim ruling; the cdoc-m1 beads add it. Under `cargo xtask ci wasm`, the lib targets of calc-doc-model and calc-doc record zero_tests, because the cases live only in the acceptance target.
Ruling after round 3 (2026-10-15/17): the round-3 judge closed the build loop with no blocking finding. The refuters' surviving mutants are test-strength defects found before the probe, so they are fixed in a further commit on this bead after the build commit, as AGENTS.md provides. They are: the frame reader defaulting a missing base, version, operations or format; a negative integer read as u64; lenient visibility, error-name or hex-unit spellings; an AxisEdit::last off-by-one; ModelRoot accessors no case observes; and FiniteNumber's bitwise equality. The same commit states the formula-length and 2^53 limits on their items and corrects two doc comments and two Display messages. The mutation probe then runs on that fix commit.
close_reason:
Product status: calc-doc-model defines CalcDoc's engine-neutral authored contract, and calc-doc re-exports it as calc_doc::model:
- AuthoredRevision;
- an immutable, Arc-shared ModelRoot of sheets (SheetId, document-stable SheetKey, SheetName, SheetVisibility);
- OpBatch of WorkbookOps (SetCell, Clear, EditAxis, EditSheet);
- CellInput (finite number, text, logical, error, formula text; never a calculated value);
- one generated wire codec per capability (cells, axes, sheets), behind a versioned envelope and frame, with exact numbers and text and a typed refusal for every unknown or malformed input.
By the claim ruling, the production route calc_doc::open/prepare_edit/prepare_save/write is absent; the cdoc-m1 beads add it.
Evidence: build commit d8570dd and fix commit 8c7eae0.
- Windows: cargo xtask accept --id cdoc-m0.1 --platform windows --require-all exit 0, "ACCEPT passed cdoc_m0_1__op_roundtrip", "ACCEPT passed cdoc_m0_1__no_engine_dependency", "2 selected, 2 passed ... architecture checks 7/7 passed".
- wasm: --platform wasm --require-all exit 0, both cases "ran in Chrome" and "ran in Firefox".
- Linux, in the WSL clone at 8c7eae0: --platform linux --require-all exit 0, "2 selected, 2 passed".
- Receipts: accept-receipts/cdoc-m0.1/{windows,wasm,linux}.json.
- The fix commit makes the cases fail on 16 mutants the refuters had left green (fix/probes-final).
- Mutation probe on 8c7eae0: 10 of 10 breaks caught.
  - A shared byte-order swap, shared text truncation and a shared corner swap failed at the golden fixtures.
  - An unknown-key fallback, admitted newer versions, a cached value beside a formula, an axis edit past the grid's end, an undispatched capability and a wrong revision accessor each failed at their rows.
  - Without the browser attribute, no_engine_dependency was missing in both browsers.
- Regressions at 8c7eae0, all exit 0: Windows accepts of infra-m0.1 (with independent_lanes), m0.2, m0.3, m0.4, m0.5, dc-e8ql and cfunc-m0.1; cfunc-m0.1's wasm accept; cargo xtask ci wasm; cargo xtask ci licenses.
Still open:
- The 50 seams entries of calc-doc-model are counted as reach unproven (dc-kzkj, before dc-pz3u).
- dc-7qtj (layering rule) and dc-85qk (Excel's sheet-name rules).
- Limits stated on their items, with owners noted on cdoc-m4.3, chost-m1.1 and cdoc-m1.2: batch-internal sheet references, key reuse, the base revision, formula length, and integers above 2^53.
- Under cargo xtask ci wasm, the lib targets of calc-doc-model and calc-doc report zero_tests, because the cases live only in the acceptance target.
- CI push run 39104574184 was in progress when this bead closed.

Sharpened at claim (2026-10-15):
- Package and route. calc-value belongs to the CalcFunc library (plan 1.3), so this bead's files are crates/calc-value and crates/calc-func. The types live in calc-value. calc-func gains a normal dependency on calc-value and re-exports it as its value API, and the two named cases live in crates/calc-func/tests/acceptance.rs, registered in crates/calc-func/acceptance.json with platforms windows, linux and wasm, so the Acceptance command `cargo test -p calc-func --test acceptance cfunc_m0_1 -- --nocapture` runs them as written. The cases reach the types only through calc-func's re-export. calc_func::invoke and the generated catalogue arrive with cfunc-m1.1; this bead adds neither, and no stand-in for them.
- Port. OxFunc crates/oxfunc_value_types/src/lib.rs at 6fca3518 (blob d79060c9fb57d6620482644dfe2b2a29d11b8ede). `cargo xtask pin-sources --lookup` exits 6 with calls_quarantined [OxFunc run-time loads]; the file's only run-time loads are in its test module wire_schema_tests (read_dir and read_to_string over the repository's own sources), which is not ported. Port CalcValue, CoreValue, ReferenceLike and WorksheetErrorCode. Drop the send-values feature and its Rc arm: calc-value declares no cargo features and Arc is its only shared pointer. Replace ReferenceLike's string-address payloads (the target text, the textual identity, the multi-area string splitting) with typed references built from SheetId and checked coordinates. Keep the value semantics that remain (the 14 worksheet error codes, Excel text as UTF-16 code units with the 32,767-unit interop truncation, array shape and row-major access, the callable arity shape). Every item of the source that is not ported (rich values, presentation hints, error metadata, ValueBoundary, the wire schema, Value and EvalError, and the rest) is listed in the migration record with its reason and the bead that will need it, or that no bead names it.
- Migration record: a new file migration/ports/cfunc-m0.1.json that only this bead writes. For each ported source: repository, commit, path and blob (equal to the pin's), the lookup exit and calls_quarantined list, each symbol ported, each semantic change with its reason, the items not ported, and the semantic witnesses changed (each OxFunc test whose expectation the port changes or drops, with the test that replaces it or the reason none does).
- IDs. WorkbookId, SheetId, NameId, TableId and NodeId are generational (slot and generation) and issued by an allocator; a released slot comes back with a new generation; a slot whose generation would wrap is retired, never reused; there is no public constructor from raw parts. Uniqueness holds among the IDs one allocator issues; identity across workbooks is the pair of WorkbookId and SheetId, a limit the record states.
- CellKey: a SheetId and u32 row and column, 1-based (rows 1 to 1,048,576, columns 1 to 16,384), private fields, checked construction with a typed error for zero and out-of-bounds coordinates. A CellKey and a full-grid area are Copy values that allocate nothing.
- Case cfunc_m0_1__grid_edges: A1 and XFD1048576 round-trip through the checked constructor and the accessors; the test decodes and re-encodes the A1 text itself (calc-value parses no A1 text; reference text belongs to CalcFml). Row 0, column 0, row 1,048,577 and column 16,385 fail with the typed error. Keys at the same row and column on distinct SheetIds (two live sheets, and a released and reissued slot) are unequal and stay distinct map keys. A counting global allocator in the test binary measures zero allocations while the edge keys and the full-grid area are built.
- Case cfunc_m0_1__send_sync: compile-time assertions that every public value type, the reference types, the IDs and the callable contract are Send + Sync, and an observable that no opt-out exists: calc-value declares no cargo features (the case reads its Cargo.toml through include_str!, so the same check runs in the browsers).
- NumericMode { Fast, Exact(NumericTargetId) } with Fast as the default (plan 5.1); NumericTargetId names the Excel build, channel and compatibility and the numeric environment (plan 5.2). No process-global mode.
- wasm: wasm-bindgen =0.2.117 and wasm-bindgen-test =0.3.67 as wasm32-only dev-dependencies of calc-func (the pair the CI browser fixture pins). Each case is #[test] natively and #[wasm_bindgen_test] on wasm32, with no browser or Node configuration of its own (the runner forces the browser with WASM_BINDGEN_USE_BROWSER). The wasm runs set CHROMEDRIVER and GECKODRIVER to chromedriver 155.0.8059.39 and geckodriver 0.37.0 in %USERPROFILE%\.cargo\bin.
- seams.json of calc-value and calc-func: every pub enum variant and pub trait listed with a non-test caller, and the registered case named for an entry executes that caller.
- Adversarial class (M0 exit bead): refuters and judge at xhigh effort, and a mutation probe after the build commit, before the push.
Rulings after round 1 (2026-10-15):
- calc-value's kept OxFunc semantic witnesses (its unit tests) run in Chrome and Firefox as well as natively: wasm-bindgen =0.2.117 and wasm-bindgen-test =0.3.67 are wasm32-only dev-dependencies of calc-value too, and each calc-value unit test is #[test] natively and #[wasm_bindgen_test] on wasm32. `cargo xtask ci wasm` is their browser evidence.
- Every not-ported entry of migration/ports/cfunc-m0.1.json names the beads that will need the item, found by a recorded search (the OxFunc files at the pin that use the symbol, the beads the pin lists for those files, and docs/plan/BEAD_DETAILS.md); rich values and presentation hints name cfunc-m3.19.
- A multi-area (union) reference holds areas of one sheet only; 3D sheet spans, structured references, spill anchors and external workbook references are not ported here and are recorded with their beads.
- dc-0oyu (created 2026-10-15, blocks dc-pz3u) points calc-value's seams entries at callers outside calc-value once consumers exist.
- The orchestrator updates the bootstrap note in AGENTS.md.
Rulings after round 3 (2026-10-15):
- Owner-search scope: the searches behind the not-ported entries match only pinned OxFunc port inputs that are not quarantined (577 files, lookup exits 0, 5 or 6), with a separate, file-name-only pass over the 391 reference inputs. Quarantined inputs are never matched, so the beads of the 7 quarantined inputs are not weighed; a port of quarantined code is not a need this record can name.
- Orchestrator data step on migration/ports/cfunc-m0.1.json after the round-3 judge: the external-workbook entry now lists the three port inputs that use allow_external_refs and names cfunc-m3.1 to cfunc-m3.21; the reference pass states the lookup exits actually seen; send_values_audit excludes this bead. Also corrected: the send_sync ACCEPT-NOTE no longer claims a thread crossing it does not make, and WorksheetErrorCode's doc comment no longer claims a complete set.
- dc-8gn8 (prerequisite of this bead's close): infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency fails once calc-func depends on calc-value, because its OS-binding expectations list calc-value alone. It lands after this build commit and before the push.
- dc-78xm: applying a result's format or style hint to its cell, and HYPERLINK's family. Notes on cfml-m3.4, cfunc-m1.1 and cfunc-m1.2 (dropped ValueBoundary witnesses), cfunc-m3.19 (HYPERLINK), cfml-m3.5 (workbook-qualified identity) and dc-0oyu (NumericMode::target, all() completeness).
close_reason:
Product status: calc-value is the first library API, re-exported by calc-func as calc_func::value. It provides:
- generational, allocator-issued WorkbookId, SheetId, NameId, TableId and NodeId;
- CellKey and GridArea with checked 1-based u32 coordinates covering A1 to XFD1048576, which allocate nothing;
- CalcValue, CoreValue, ReferenceLike (typed areas of one sheet), WorksheetErrorCode, ExcelText, CalcArray and CallableValue, held in Arc and Send + Sync, with no cargo features;
- NumericMode { Fast (default), Exact(NumericTargetId) }.
It is ported from OxFunc oxfunc_value_types at 6fca3518, recorded in migration/ports/cfunc-m0.1.json.
Evidence: build commit 98f99fd, plus dc-8gn8's 1416d1c, which keeps infra-m0.3's case green with the new dependency.
- Windows: cargo xtask accept --id cfunc-m0.1 --platform windows --require-all exit 0, "ACCEPT passed cfunc_m0_1__send_sync", "ACCEPT passed cfunc_m0_1__grid_edges", "2 selected, 2 passed ... architecture checks 7/7 passed".
- wasm: --platform wasm --require-all exit 0. Both cases "ran in Chrome" and "ran in Firefox" (chromedriver 155.0.8059.39, geckodriver 0.37.0).
- Linux, in the WSL clone at 1416d1c: --platform linux --require-all exit 0, "2 selected, 2 passed". Receipts: accept-receipts/cfunc-m0.1/{windows,wasm,linux}.json.
- calc-value's 18 kept witnesses: cargo test -p calc-value --lib "18 passed". CI run 38724812987 (artifact ci-wasm, commit 1416d1c) shows "Running headless tests in Chrome" and "Running headless tests in Firefox", each followed by "test result: ok. 18 passed".
- Mutation probe on 98f99fd: 8 of 8 breaks caught. grid_edges failed on the row bound 1,048,577, on the generation bump (with 3 unit tests), on sheet-blind CellKey equality, on an allocation in GridArea::full_sheet and on a cross-sheet union (with its unit test). send_sync failed on deep-copied text and on a private Rc. Dropping the browser attribute left grid_edges missing in both browsers.
- Regressions at 1416d1c, Windows: infra-m0.1 (incl. independent_lanes), infra-m0.2, infra-m0.3, infra-m0.4, infra-m0.5 and dc-e8ql accepts, and cargo xtask ci wasm, all exit 0.
- CI push run 38724812987 is green.
Still open:
- The 32 seams entries have callers only inside calc-value and are counted as reach unproven (dc-0oyu, before dc-pz3u).
- dc-78xm: format hints and HYPERLINK's family.
- dc-tj29.
- Notes on cfml-m3.4, cfunc-m1.1, cfunc-m1.2, cfunc-m3.19 and cfml-m3.5.
- IDs are unique per allocator only (cfml-m3.5 decides workbook-qualified identity).
- On wasm, send_sync rests on compile-time bounds, because wasm32-unknown-unknown has no threads.

Every entry of crates/calc-value/seams.json names a caller outside calc-value that its named acceptance case reaches, so calc-value meets dc-pz3u's rule that a caller inside the defining library does not count.

## Context
Follow-up of cfunc-m0.1 (2026-10-15, round-1 judge). cfunc-m0.1 listed 32 seams entries (the variants of IdError, GridError, ReferenceError, CoreValue, WorksheetErrorCode and NumericMode, and the OpaqueCallable trait) whose only callers are inside calc-value, because no package consumes calc-value at M0. Thirteen WorksheetErrorCode variants are named only by WorksheetErrorCode::all(), which only tests call, and the case named for IdError::Exhausted never produces that variant (the allocator's slot limit is u32::MAX). The expected first consumers are cdoc-m0.1 (its operation codec encodes literal values and error codes), cfunc-m1.1 (the call interface), cfml-m1.1 and ceng-m1.1. CalcFunc files only.

## Do
Once those consumers exist, point each calc-value entry at a consumer caller and at a registered case that reaches it. A variant that still has no consumer is either removed or given a bead that adds its caller; the receipt counts the entries still waiting and names those beads.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id cfunc-m0.1 --platform windows --require-all
```
The seams check reports no calc-value entry whose only caller is inside calc-value, and every remaining wait is counted with its bead.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux for repository/tooling execution.

## Out of scope
Changing the seams check itself (dc-pz3u).
notes:
Also from cfunc-m0.1's round-3 judge: NumericMode::target() has no non-test caller either. WorksheetErrorCode::all() is checked only through its fixed-length array, so a variant added to the enum but left out of all() still passes; add a test whose exhaustive match fails in that case.

From cdoc-m0.1 (2026-10-15): crates/calc-doc-model/src/wire/value.rs names all 14 WorksheetErrorCode variants in non-test code (the wire names of error literals), a caller outside calc-value for those entries.

## Context

A search of docs/plan/BEAD_DETAILS.md for presentation hints and number formats found no bead that applies a result's hint to its cell's displayed or saved format. FUNC.HYPERLINK (OxFunc crates/oxfunc_core/src/functions/hyperlink_fn.rs, pinned for cfunc-m3.1 to cfunc-m3.21) uses the style hint, and no family of the source manifest lists it. Libraries: CalcFml formatting and CalcHost projection; the bead that takes it decides the split.

## Do
Decide where a result's hint becomes the cell's effective format (Excel applies it only when the cell's format is General) and implement it on the production route, with a live-Excel witness for NOW, TODAY and HYPERLINK. Also rule whether cfunc-m3.19's term 'link' covers HYPERLINK, or add it to a family.

## Port from

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id dc-78xm --platform windows --require-all
```
A NOW() cell with General format displays as a date and saves with a date number format, and a HYPERLINK cell takes the hyperlink style, each matched against an Excel capture.

title: Scope goal: distributed, billion-node, typed and debuggable computation on Excel formulas
description:
## Outcome
DNA Calc stays based on Excel formulas, Excel functions and Excel's extensibility (LAMBDA, UDFs, add-ins). On that base it also offers what the owner's reference platform offers (Jane Street's Webs, a distributed, spreadsheet-like computation platform):
1. Distributed computation of one calculation domain across machines.
2. Incremental recomputation that scales to billions of nodes and edges, with recalculation work proportional to what changed.
3. Strong typing and rich data structures beyond traditional spreadsheet values, while the formula language stays Excel's.
4. Computations defined and edited both from Rust and from a web interface, through the same host route.
5. A formula debugger in the web interface that shows how a formula evaluated, on the one evaluator.
6. Performance at that scale, recorded with named scale workloads.

## Context
Recorded at the owner's request (2026-10-17) as a further scope goal. It is not part of the first version as plan section 11.2 and the plan header define it, and recording it changes no plan decision. The owner decides its placement (Owner questions below). The read-only mapping workflow wf_a31948f5-14a (2026-10-17) compared the goal with the plan, the tracker and the code; its findings follow.

Groundwork that exists:
- Engine state is supplied by the caller, and recalculation runs in budgeted steps (plan 2.2). Values, plans and input snapshots are immutable, Arc-shared and Send + Sync, and later frame-level parallelism against one snapshot is described (plan 3.5; cfunc_m0_1__send_sync).
- An evaluation step can request a dependency that is not ready, or yield (plan 2.2, 6.2). Async completions, pending-result tokens and external updates are versioned session operations (plan 8.8; cfml-m4.3, ceng-m4.6, chost-m4.11). Function metadata declares volatility, thread safety and async (cfunc-m4.1).
- Graph nodes exist only for formulas and participants, never for every coordinate. Ranges become interval edges, scheduling uses a ready queue with prerequisite counts and SCC condensation, an edit copies only bounded pages, and plans are shared across instances (plan 3.2, 4.1, 6.1, 6.2). Structural counters check all of this (infra-m7.8).
- Fast is deterministic across platforms, with identical effect tapes and bits (plan 5.4), so distributed results can be required to replay.
- The operation wire codec is versioned and exact, and names sheets by document-stable SheetKeys (cdoc-m0.1).
- Host dispatch is the one route for every caller, automation included (plan 2.2; chost-m4.12). Auditing must instrument the one evaluator (chost-m6.3), which is what a debugger needs.

Plan decisions the goal cuts across (owner decisions):
- One evaluator and one graph. Each workbook's mutation and calculation lane is serial, and no second parallel graph or evaluator is prebuilt in this phase (honesty rule 5; plan 3.5). Section 6 is the single-threaded reference strategy. Later strategies are admitted only behind the same operations and evaluator, checked by the differential twin (plan 6.5; ceng-m7.1). Distribution therefore has to be one graph partitioned under one ordered commit authority per domain (plan 3.3). It cannot be federated engines that exchange values in rounds (plan 6.1; ceng-m3.9).
- Excel only, with one formula language and no second DSL (executive decision; plan 4.2). Types must therefore be Excel's own (richData, entity and linked data types) or have an Excel-visible projection. A Rust definition API must produce Excel formulas, defined names and registered functions, because a computation lives in a cell or a defined name (plan header; 8.2).
- Persistence is xlsx with no sidecar, inside Excel's fixed grid (plan 8.2; calc-value grid bounds), so billions of nodes means many sheets, names or workbooks.
- No performance targets: measurements are recorded without thresholds, and a number is never called fast (plan header, 5.4, 10.4, 10.5; work prompt honesty inventory).
- Fast forbids uncontrolled reassociation (plan 5.4), so parallel or distributed reductions must keep a fixed order to stay replayable. Exact is native x86-64 only (plan 5.2).
- Portable packages cannot import networking (plan 1.3; os-imports check), so transport belongs in a native-only package under platform/.
- The browser hosts its own engine in a wasm32 worker (plan 3.5; dnacalc-m2.1). A web interface onto a shared or remote computation is a new host mode the plan does not describe.

Foreclosure risks in code that exists or comes next, cheapest to decide now:
- calc-value IDs (cfunc-m0.1, closed) are a u32 slot plus a u32 generation, which caps one workbook at about 4.29 billion node slots; the plan's sketch had u64. Slots live in a dense Vec, and calc-value declares no cargo features, so widening later breaks every consumer (crates/calc-value/src/id.rs).
- IDs are unique per allocator only, and NodeId has no document-stable key. Callable identity is a process-local Arc (crates/calc-value/src/value.rs). Cross-machine node and LAMBDA identity need a design.
- CoreValue is an exhaustive enum with no extension slot, and the 21 function-family ports will match on it. ArrayShape is usize, which is 32 bits on wasm32.
- ceng-m1.1 (the next engine bead) decides whether input pages are reached by in-process borrows or through a page-handle interface a remote partition could serve.
- cfml-m1.3 (a bottleneck bead) decides the plan and frame layout. Without an observation hook and a source-span map, a step debugger later means changing the evaluator. chost-m6.3 relies on a CalcFml trace policy that no bead owns.
- cfunc-m3.23 and cfunc-m3.4 decide the reduction order of aggregates under Fast.
- dnacalc-m2.1 decides whether its transport is independent of where the host runs.
- RecalcFacts is whole per-generation vectors (plan 2.2). AuthoredRevision is one u64 counter with one base per batch, which means one writer. ModelRoot handles sheets linearly (cdoc-m0.1), which is harmless at Excel's sheet counts.

## Do
An epic holds no work. Once the owner places this goal, a planning bead derives its child beads (as infra-m3.20 to infra-m3.24 do) and attaches them at these points:
- ceng-m7.1's strategy layer;
- ceng-m3.9's calculation domain;
- the async route of cfml-m4.3 and ceng-m4.6;
- dnacalc-m2.1's transport and a native-only transport package under platform/;
- chost-m4.12's programmatic route;
- auditing in chost-m6.3 and dnacalc-m6.19;
- infra-m7.8's named workloads;
- typed values in cdoc-m3.4, infra-m3.23 and cfunc-m3.19.

## Owner questions
1. Placement: a phase after the first version (after infra-m8.2), or do parts of it enter earlier?
2. ID width: keep calc-value's u32 slots, or widen them to u64 before cdoc-m0.1 closes and before ceng-m1.1 builds on them?
3. Typed values: exactly Excel's own data types, so that Excel opens them, or a DNA extension? And does CoreValue gain an extension slot now?
4. Performance: keep recorded workloads without thresholds, or set targets for named scale workloads? Targets would lift a plan rule.
5. Determinism: must parallel and distributed results stay bit-identical to the serial reference? A yes fixes the reduction order.
6. Anchoring: may a Rust-defined computation exist without a cell or defined-name anchor? The plan header and section 8.2 say no today.
7. Persistence: must every computation still open in Excel, or is a second store admitted for billion-node graphs?
8. Debugger timing: does formula auditing (chost-m6.3, M6, P3) move earlier, and which bead owns the CalcFml trace policy?

## Out of scope
Any change to the first version's scope, to the plan text or to build_plan.py until the owner rules on the questions above.
notes:
Owner rulings (2026-10-18):
- Question 2, ID width, is answered with option 1. calc-value keeps its 32-bit slots, and no ID is widened. Excel-size workbooks sit two to three orders of magnitude below the cap of about 4.29 billion slots per kind per workbook, and memory runs out long before that. Compact 32-bit slots keep the engine's edge lists small. If this goal is ever placed, scale beyond one process comes from partitioning the graph: each partition has its own allocator and graph, and a cross-partition reference is a (partition, NodeId) pair. A distributed graph needs that layer whatever the slot width.
- Scope guard: no work items and no design go down this goal's path beyond what Excel scope needs. The epic stays deferred. No bead adds Webs-specific abstractions, interfaces, APIs, workloads or extension slots, such as remote page access, a remote host transport, partition-aware IDs, DNA-only typed values or billion-node workloads, unless the owner places this epic. The notes on the attachment beads were narrowed to Excel-scope choices on the same day.

title: Keep infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency's OS-binding scenarios independent of the stand-in package's dependents
description:
## Outcome
infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency passes on a workspace in which portable packages depend on calc-value, because its OS-binding scenarios no longer depend on which packages happen to depend on the package that carries the stand-in crate.

## Context
Prerequisite of cfunc-m0.1's close (2026-10-15). cfunc-m0.1 adds calc-func's dependency on calc-value. The OS-binding scenarios of infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency (tools/xtask/tests/acceptance/infra_m0_3.rs, the `binding` table near line 1655) attach a stand-in `winapi` crate to crates/calc-value and expect exactly calc-value's lines. With the new edge, the check also reports, correctly, that portable calc-func has winapi in its wasm32-unknown-unknown closure, so os-binding-direct and os-binding-transitive each gain one line and the case fails ('failures: 2', round-3 refuter of cfunc-m0.1). The check is right; the expectation is too narrow. Infrastructure files only (tools/xtask).

## Do
Attach the stand-in to a portable package that no workspace member may depend on, such as apps/dna-onecalc, or compute the expected lines from the copy's resolved metadata (the stand-in package plus each portable package whose closure reaches it). In either case, assert that every line the check prints names a package whose closure really contains the stand-in. Keep every other scenario of the case unchanged.

notes:

close_reason:

title: Run registered acceptance cases in CI on every push
description:
## Outcome
A push to master runs every closed bead's registered acceptance cases that can run on the CI hosts, so a regression in any case turns CI red, and the cases that need local resources are listed as not run with their reason.

## Context
Follow-up from the infra-m0.2 judge (2026-10-14): `cargo xtask ci windows` and `ci linux` exclude every package's acceptance target (tools/xtask/src/ci.rs:667-698, 1162-1190, 1312-1320); acceptance cases run in CI only through the workflow_dispatch accept_ids input. The reasons are sound (ACCEPT-NOT-RUN reads as passed under plain cargo test; infra_m0_1__independent_lanes needs a clean checkout; infra-m0.4's cases need the legacy repositories; the cases would recurse), so the route is the runner itself. Infrastructure files only.

## Do
On push, run `cargo xtask accept --id <id> --platform <job> --require-all` for every bead whose cases declare that platform, in an order that keeps the checkout clean for cases that need it, record each receipt, fail the job on any failed case, and list not_run cases (for example infra-m0.4 without the legacy repositories) with their reason in the job summary.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.2 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.2 --platform linux --require-all
```
A push CI run's artifacts hold a receipt for every closed bead with cases on that platform; a deliberately failing case in a fixture bead turns the job red.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux for repository/tooling execution.

## Out of scope
Oracle (excel) cases, which only the owner runs.

title: Prove the runner's wasm route runs real browsers
description:
## Outcome
`cargo xtask accept --platform wasm` records a case as passed in Chromium or Firefox only when that browser actually ran it, so cfunc-m0.1's wasm evidence is browser evidence and never a Node.js run.

## Context
Prerequisite of cfunc-m0.1, the first bead that declares wasm cases. Found by the infra-m0.3 refuters (2026-10-14): the wasm route sets only CARGO_TARGET_WASM32_UNKNOWN_UNKNOWN_RUNNER and CHROMEDRIVER or GECKODRIVER (tools/xtask/src/accept.rs:499-507); nothing forces a browser, and the outcome classifier never checks which browser ran (accept.rs:193-248). The excel and wasm not_run branches (Excel not registered, runner or driver missing; accept.rs:417-426, 464, 1016-1019) are exercised by no test. Infrastructure files only (tools/xtask). Plan section 10.4: a wasm compile-only job is not browser validation.

## Do
Force browser execution for every wasm run and confirm from the runner's own output which browser executed each case; record that per browser in the receipt. Prove that `--list` and `--exact` select exactly one case under wasm-bindgen-test-runner. Add unit tests with an injected probe for each not_run branch (Excel absent, runner missing, driver missing). Install chromedriver matching the installed Chrome if the proof needs it, and name it in the commit message. Agents never run `--platform excel`.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id dc-e8ql --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id dc-e8ql --platform linux --require-all
```
- `dc_e8ql__browser_route` (registered under dc-e8ql in tools/xtask/acceptance.json, platforms windows and linux): a fixture wasm case that is not configured for a browser is recorded failed, never `<case>@chromium passed`; a fixture wasm case run in both browsers is recorded passed per browser with the browser's banner in its log; --list and --exact select exactly one case. On a host without the runner or drivers the case asserts the not_run outcome with its reason. Unit tests (`cargo test -p xtask --bins`) show each not_run branch with its reason.
## Platforms
Windows and Linux for repository/tooling execution; the browser fixture runs on this Windows PC with Chrome and Firefox.

## Out of scope
CI (infra-m0.2); cfunc-m0.1's own cases.
notes:
Sharpened at claim (2026-10-14):
- Toolchain on this PC: Chrome 155.0.8059.40, Firefox 151.0.3, geckodriver 0.37.0 and wasm-bindgen-test-runner 0.2.117 in %USERPROFILE%\.cargo\bin. The orchestrator installed chromedriver 155.0.8059.39 there at claim, from Google's Chrome-for-Testing storage (the closest listed build of major version 155); the build commit names it. wasm-bindgen-test-runner requires the wasm-bindgen crate at exactly its own version, so the fixture pins wasm-bindgen =0.2.117 and a matching wasm-bindgen-test. The WSL Ubuntu clone has no browser, driver or runner. Node.js is installed on both Windows and WSL, so an unconfigured wasm test can run under Node and must not be scored as a browser pass.
- This bead gets its own case, dc_e8ql__browser_route, registered in tools/xtask/acceptance.json under id dc-e8ql with platforms windows and linux. It holds the browser scenarios, and its receipts are accept-receipts/dc-e8ql/<platform>.json, so infra-m0.3's committed receipts stay as its close cites them. Acceptance: `cargo xtask accept --id dc-e8ql --platform windows --require-all` and `--platform linux --require-all`.
- The case builds a fixture package with one wasm case in a temporary workspace copy, then runs `accept --id <fixture bead> --platform wasm --require-all` through the real runner. On a host with both drivers it must show three things. (1) Each browser recorded passed only when the runner's own output names that browser: a forced-browser setting (for example WASM_BINDGEN_USE_BROWSER), plus a check of the banner wasm-bindgen-test-runner prints ("Running headless tests in Chrome/Firefox" or the like). (2) A fixture case that is not configured for a browser is never recorded `<case>@chromium passed`. (3) --list and --exact select exactly one case under the runner. On a host without drivers (the WSL clone) the same scenario asserts the missing-driver not_run outcome, with its reason. The receipt states which branch ran, so the Linux pass proves the not_run branch, and only the Windows pass proves real browsers.
- Unit tests inject the probes for every not_run branch: Excel not registered, runner missing, and each driver missing.
- Agents never run --platform excel.
close_reason:
Product status: the runner's wasm route forces browser execution (WASM_BINDGEN_USE_BROWSER=1, the other browser's driver variables removed) and records a browser's run as passed only under that browser's own runner banner; a 1-passed Node.js run is failed. Per-browser receipt entries record browser, banner, driver environment and executed_in (format dnacalc-accept-receipt/4). chromedriver 155.0.8059.39 installed for Chrome 155.0.8059.40. Build commit 6e904a2, pushed.
Evidence: Windows (rustc/cargo 1.94.1, chromedriver 155.0.8059.39, geckodriver 0.37.0, wasm-bindgen-test-runner 0.2.117), accept-receipts/dc-e8ql/windows.json: "ACCEPT passed dc_e8ql__browser_route (package xtask, exit code 0)", RESULT passed, architecture checks 6/6, exit code 0; its notes record branch browsers: fixture_browser__alpha@chromium passed under "Running headless tests in Chrome" with user agent HeadlessChrome/155, @firefox passed under "Running headless tests in Firefox" with user agent Firefox/151, fixture_browser_node__alpha reported 1 passed under Node.js/25 and was recorded failed in both browsers, and the pre-change route had run the same fixture under Node.js and reported it passed. cargo test -p xtask --bins 62 passed (each not_run branch), fmt, clippy -D warnings, infra_m0_1__agent_contract 1 passed, infra-m0.3 Windows regression passed (its receipt restored unchanged). Linux (WSL Ubuntu, rustc/cargo 1.93.1, clone at 6e904a2), accept-receipts/dc-e8ql/linux.json: dc_e8ql__browser_route passed, RESULT passed, exit code 0, branch not_run (wasm-bindgen-test-runner not on PATH, so no real browser is proven on Linux; the driver-missing branch with a runner present is unit-tested only).
Still open: dc-pih5 (driver variables, banner position, versions in receipts, pinned fixture lock, driver-missing scenario with a runner present).

title: Harden the source scans, build-script link rules and the CalcFunc layering rule
description:
## Outcome
The os-imports and tree-reference-tokens checks of `cargo xtask accept` cannot be passed by spelling changes, a portable build script cannot link a native library, calc-value has its own layering rule, and the forbidden-dependency case says when it cannot test its named pair directly.

## Context
Follow-up from the infra-m0.3 refuters (2026-10-14). Known bypasses: `use std::{self as host}; host::fs::read(..)` passes os-imports (tools/xtask/src/arch.rs:423, 492); filesystem methods on std::path types are not denied; `extern "C"` blocks without #[link] pass (tools/xtask/architecture.json:49); `cargo::rustc-link-lib` in a portable build.rs passes every check (arch.rs:545-554); tree-reference-tokens misses single-case joined spellings such as treeref, TREEREF and referenceprofile (tools/xtask/src/text.rs:42-69); only calc-func carries the CalcFunc layering rule (architecture.json:3-8). Once calc-host depends on calc-fml (plan section 2.1), infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency silently picks another package for its calc-host into calc-fml scenario (tools/xtask/tests/acceptance/infra_m0_3.rs:1236-1266), and its assertion at :1319 cannot fail. Orchestrator rulings: portable build scripts may use std::fs (catalogue generation needs it) but no rustc-link-lib, rustc-link-search or rustc-link-arg directive; the tree-token scan of doc comments stays (stricter than the round-1 ruling). Infrastructure files only (tools/xtask).

## Do
Close each bypass above with a rejecting fixture: std aliasing, std::path filesystem calls, extern blocks of any ABI without an allow-listed reason, the three build-script link directives, joined single-case tree tokens. Add a calc-value rule (it depends on no other workspace package) with a rejecting scenario. When the named calc-host into calc-fml pair would form a cycle, assert that cargo rejects the cycle and record that in the receipt instead of substituting a package; make the dna-onecalc assertion able to fail.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.3 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.3 --platform linux --require-all
```
Each bypass above has a fixture that makes its check fail; the calc-value scenario exits 1 with the rule named.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux for repository/tooling execution.

The seams coverage proof (dc-pz3u); the word scan.

title: Strengthen the source-manifest case checks and lookup exit codes
description:

The recorded working_tree uses STATUS_CONFIG (tools/xtask/src/pin_git.rs:18) and differs from plain `git status --porcelain` without saying so. `--lookup` exits 0 for both port and reference inputs, 1 for an empty argument instead of 2 (pin.rs:2404), and prints neither `uses` nor `quarantined_helpers` for the 51 port inputs that call the quarantined excel_numeric dispatcher (pin.rs:2494). on_origin comes from local remote-tracking refs without a fetch (pin.rs:497) and the manifest rules do not say so. title: Derive infra-m0.5's tainted-commit list by rule, check it at accept time, and review ffcb9a77
description:
## Outcome
migration/numeric-provenance.json's tainted_commits list is derived from a rule the record states, the infra-m0.5 case recomputes it from `git log` at the pinned commit and fails when a commit is missing, and an independent reviewer's verdict on OxFunc commit ffcb9a77 is recorded by that reviewer, so infra-m0.5 can close.

## Context
Prerequisite of infra-m0.5, holding its close (2026-10-15). infra-m0.5's round-3 judge left two blocking findings after the third implementer round: (1) the tainted-commit list was hand-picked (16 commits) while the record's own reasons name a class (W108/W109 identification commits) that `git log -i -E --grep='W10[89].*identif|identif.*(graph|staging)|IDENTIFIED' 6fca3518` finds 64 of, and the case only checks that five named commits are present (tools/xtask/tests/acceptance/infra_m0_5.rs:1216-1235); (2) the implementer alone decided not to list ffcb9a77, which modified excel_numeric/x87.rs and mod.rs and added smart-fuzzer/tools/w111/complex_kernel_probe (a tainted class) as well as the W111 captures. As a conservative data fix the orchestrator listed every commit matching the stated rule (identification commits, and every commit whose message holds one of the record's 15 sweep patterns: 70 commits) plus ffcb9a77, pending this bead. Infrastructure files only. The infra-m0.5 reading rule applies.

## Do
State the derivation rule in the record and make `cargo xtask pin-sources` and the accept-time check derive the list from git at the pin, failing on any omission; run an independent review (a separate reviewer agent, its verbatim output committed) of ffcb9a77 and of every commit the rule adds, with witness independence argued from the capture files' own acquisition, not from a commit being unlisted; apply the verdicts; remove from both migration files the remaining staging residue (the 87disp control-word value and the helper instruction sequences quoted at numeric-provenance.json:76, 130-141, 163, 343-344, and the staging tokens listed in infra_m0_5.rs:68, 1814), keeping only citing clauses; settle the disposition of extended-numeric/numeric-outcomes.json and check, rather than assert, that it was written before the freeze steps.

## Port from
fresh

```text
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.5 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.5 --platform linux --require-all
```

## Platforms
Windows and Linux for repository/tooling execution.

## Out of scope
Clearing any catalogue file (dc-2203).
notes:
Sharpened at claim (2026-10-15):
- Order: an independent review first, then the implementer round. The review is a separate, read-only reviewer agent whose verbatim structured output is committed as migration/numeric-provenance-review-2026-10-15-commits.json. It gives a verdict on ffcb9a77 and on each of the 55 commits the stated rule added. For every file the witness chain depends on, it says whether that file's own acquisition evidence shows black-box Excel capture independent of the tainted research that ffcb9a77 also carries: the five answer captures, extended-numeric/numeric-outcomes.json and its writer retain_numeric_campaign.py, the runner Run-W109BulkBatch.ps1 at the blob that ran, CellRefBatch.psm1, run_numeric_campaign.py, the input generator, and the snapshot and freeze scripts. It also checks the ordering claim, that the retention was written before the freeze steps.
- Precedence change: a file changed by a listed tainted commit stays at least unresolved unless a reviewed per-file entry clears it and names that commit as considered. The witness chain is admitted only through such entries.

title: Harden the wasm route's browser evidence: driver variables, banner position, versions and a pinned fixture lock
description:
## Outcome
A wasm browser pass in a receipt names the exact runner, driver and browser versions that produced it, cannot be produced by a spoofed banner or a stray driver variable, and is built from a pinned dependency closure.

## Context
Follow-up from the dc-e8ql judge (2026-10-14). WASM_REMOVED (tools/xtask/src/accept.rs:644-657) does not clear CHROMEDRIVER_REMOTE, GECKODRIVER_REMOTE, MSEDGEDRIVER, the <DRIVER>_ARGS variables or WASM_BINDGEN_TEST_WEBDRIVER_JSON, which wasm-bindgen-test-runner 0.2.117 reads, and environment_removed in the receipt is that constant rather than a measured value (accept.rs:163-167). The banner check trusts the first non-empty stdout line (accept.rs:248), so a module that prints a banner-like line before the harness is not covered. The banner wording is runner-version specific and no version is recorded; per-browser entries record no runner, driver or browser version. The browser fixture's transitive dependencies float and resolve on each run (tools/xtask/tests/fixtures/browser/package.toml). Notes from both browsers are concatenated without a browser label (accept.rs:777-780), and a unit test covers an unreachable wasm host-mismatch state (accept.rs:1683). Targets configured with run_in_node_experimental still run under Node.js and are refused only by the banner check (accept.rs:639). The Linux receipt proves the runner-missing branch, not the driver-missing branch with a runner present. Infrastructure files only (tools/xtask).

## Do
Clear and record every driver variable the runner reads; check the banner's position relative to the harness output; record the runner, driver and browser versions in each per-browser entry and refuse an unknown runner version; commit a lock for the browser fixture; label notes per browser; drop the unreachable test state; add a scenario with the runner present and both drivers absent.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id dc-e8ql --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id dc-e8ql --platform linux --require-all
```
Unit tests: a spoofed banner before the harness output is refused; a stray GECKODRIVER during the chromium run does not change the browser named. Each per-browser receipt entry carries runner, driver and browser versions.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux for repository/tooling execution; the browser scenarios run on the owner's Windows PC.

## Out of scope
CI (infra-m0.2).
notes: Added from the infra-m0.2 round-2 judge (2026-10-14): the ci_matrix fixture's wasm dependency closure is re-resolved without --locked on every copy (tools/xtask/tests/acceptance/infra_m0_3.rs:427-431) and `cargo xtask ci licenses` does not review it; commit a lock for that fixture too.

description:

title: Harden infra-m0.5's numeric-provenance check
description:
## Outcome
The numeric-provenance check of `cargo xtask accept` covers what infra-m0.5's round-3 refuters found it trusts or skips, each gap closed or counted with an owner.

## Context
Follow-ups from the infra-m0.5 round-3 judge (2026-10-15). The review binding hash (status.review.dispositions_hash) was recorded by the implementer and covers only modules and classes, not rules, tainted_commits or the sweep patterns (tools/xtask/src/provenance.rs:836-872, 2043-2054, 2111-2126). 22 allowlisted files that call the stored x87 helpers (excel_x87_add/sub/mul/div/recip; for example combin.rs, depreciation_family.rs, asin.rs) are admitted as call-only although the record calls research-tool identifications generated descendants. derive() treats the ruling's tainted include case as at least unresolved (provenance.rs:1277-1355). An include of a file that is neither pinned nor reviewed is treated as clean (provenance.rs:1251-1264, 1333-1336). The accept-time witness check trusts declared builds_or_runs, names_packages, compared_rows and matched_rows and misses smart-fuzzer/engine (package sf, which depends on oxfunc_core), sweeping pinned blobs 0db00e6d and 0dc99904 rather than the blobs that ran (9fc3d4ae, 55085b4d) (provenance.rs:2374-2453). Three assertions in tools/xtask/tests/acceptance/infra_m0_5.rs (1253-1269, 3035-3063, 3064-3085) run the test's own helpers on in-memory edits instead of fixture-driven runs of the product check. The manifest's port count (851) includes 279 port inputs whose provenance is unresolved. tools/xtask/src/words.rs:561-599 allows masked occurrences of the bead-fixed case identifier in acceptance files and needs recording under dc-0nvp's baseline. pin-sources once failed with "the tainted commit ed9f2227... is not a commit of this repository" (pin.rs:704-709), cause unknown. The review file's "only change is the redactions" claim cannot be checked because no hash of the verbatim output was kept. dc-2203's text still describes the removed numeric-callers class. Infrastructure files only.

## Do
Have the reviewer record the binding hash, and extend it to rules, tainted_commits and the sweep patterns; decide stored-x87 callers' disposition; default unpinned, unreviewed includes to unresolved; re-derive witness generator facts from the blobs that ran; replace the in-memory assertions with fixture runs; count unresolved port inputs apart from port; record the word-scan exception; reproduce or explain the ed9f2227 failure; rewrite dc-2203's Outcome and Acceptance for the citation-sweep, tainted-commit and include-of-quarantined inputs.

fresh

```text

cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.5 --platform linux --require-all
```

Fixture runs show each closed gap; the manifest summary counts unresolved port inputs separately.

Windows and Linux for repository/tooling execution.

The tainted-commit rule and the ffcb9a77 review (the prerequisite bead).
notes:

(1) The tainted-commit rule is in scope here, despite the Out of scope line: the accept-time architecture check reads the rule sets from the manifest and never runs git (tools/xtask/src/provenance.rs:2038). Fixture 08b in tools/xtask/tests/acceptance/infra_m0_5.rs (3320-3325) asserts that gap exists, so invert 08b when you close it. (2) The check compares the manifest's tainted_commit_rule with the record by repository and pattern, never by pinned commit (provenance.rs:2419-2428); add a fixture whose rule sets were recorded at another commit. Added from the dc-m33w round-3 judge (2026-10-15): (7) holds_expected_bits (tools/xtask/src/provenance.rs:1371-1390) reads the witnesses section, which reviewed_view does not hash; a coordinated edit repointing a retention at a chain script's blob would lift that entry with the hash unchanged. title: Fail CI's wasm job when a package's native tests never ran in a browser

2. The native-only packages (calc-platform-desktop, calc-oracle-excel, xtask) carry compile_error! under cfg(target_arch = "wasm32"). No named case asserts that refusal yet: removing a compile_error! leaves every infra-m0.1 case green. Add the assertion to the architecture checks.

4. infra-m0.1 created the manifest format (AGENTS.md, Workspace section): per-package acceptance.json {"package", "beads": [{"id", "cases", "commands"}]}, cases in tests/acceptance.rs (test target `acceptance`). The runner extends the format (platforms, test target) and replaces the bootstrap form `cargo test -p <package> --test acceptance -- --exact <case> --nocapture`.
5. The default unit-test and doc-test harnesses of every library package print "running 0 tests"; the runner must never count them as executed cases.
6. The runner selects cases by --id. infra_m0_1__independent_lanes fails on any checkout that is off master or has uncommitted files, because it clones HEAD, so an unfiltered `cargo test -p xtask` fails during a later bead's pre-commit work. Never answer that with #[ignore].
7. Banned-word scan: docs/plan/ULTRACODE_WORK_PROMPT_OPUS_5_5.md states the rule and so contains both words; several imported tracker titles use the banned process noun (this bead's own title, infra-m3.20 to infra-m3.24 and others), and the case name infra_m0_5__quarantine_gate is a fixed identity. A registered name absent from --list (misspelled), a run with 0 tests, an ignored or filtered-out case, a failed case, or a missing platform each makes the run fail under --require-all. Default unit-test and doc-test harnesses that print "running 0 tests" never count.
- Not run: a case that cannot run on this host prints one line `ACCEPT-NOT-RUN: <case>: <reason>` (missing Excel, missing browser driver, missing capture) and the runner records it as not_run, red under --require-all. The marker can only downgrade a pass, never make one; no #[ignore].
- Host and platform: windows runs on a Windows host, linux on a Linux host, excel on a Windows host and records not_run when Excel is absent (the owner runs it; agents never invoke --platform excel), wasm runs the package's acceptance target for wasm32-unknown-unknown under wasm-bindgen-test-runner in both Chromium (CHROMEDRIVER) and Firefox (GECKODRIVER) and records not_run for a missing driver. The wasm route is first exercised by cfunc-m0.1; until then it is reported as not exercised, not as proven.
- Cargo started by the runner uses its own target directory (target/xtask-accept), never target/.
- Receipt: machine-readable JSON per run: bead, platform, host OS and architecture, rustc and cargo versions, HEAD, whether the tree was dirty and, if so, each dirty path with its git blob hash, the architecture-check results, and per case: package, argv, exit code, the libtest result line, outcome (passed, failed, not_run, missing, ignored), duration and log path. Written to target/accept/<bead>/<platform>/ and copied to the committed small path accept-receipts/<bead>/<platform>.json, which goes into the build commit for platforms run before it and into the close commit for platforms run after it (AGENTS.md updated to say the close commit carries .beads/issues.jsonl plus those receipts). The runner prints one line per case with outcome and exit code for close reasons to quote.
- Every `accept` run first runs the architecture checks and the word scan, whatever the --id, and records them in the receipt:
  (a) dependency rules of plan section 1.3 on resolved cargo metadata, for the host target and wasm32-unknown-unknown with all features: calc-func depends on none of calc-fml, calc-engine, calc-host; calc-fml on none of calc-engine, calc-host, calc-doc; calc-engine on none of calc-doc, calc-host, dna-onecalc, dna-calc; dna-onecalc's transitive closure contains neither calc-engine nor calc-host; no portable package's closure contains a native-only package;
  (b) prohibited OS imports (the infra_m0_1__workspace_builds clause): portable packages' non-test sources use no std::fs, std::process, std::os, std::net, `extern "system"` or #[link], and their resolved dependencies include no OS-binding crate from a reviewed deny list (windows, windows-sys, winapi and the like);
  (c) native-only packages refuse wasm32: each native-only package fails to compile for wasm32-unknown-unknown;
  (d) tree-reference tokens from a reviewed deny list seeded from plan sections 1.1, 1.3, 4.2 and 11.1 (tree reference, TreeRef, tree_ref, reference profile, ReferenceProfile, profile_id, ReferenceSystemProvider, host reference and their case variants) are absent from portable sources;
  (e) dead seams: each portable library package keeps a reviewed seams.json; every pub enum variant and pub trait in its non-test sources (parsed, not grepped) must be listed with at least one non-test call site that the check finds, and with the acceptance case that executes that caller (plan section 8.8: a manifest is necessary but insufficient);
  (f) word scan: the two banned words of docs/plan/ULTRACODE_WORK_PROMPT_OPUS_5_5.md section 0 over docs/, AGENTS.md, README.md, tracker text (titles, descriptions, notes, close reasons) and commit messages. Fixed identifiers such as infra_m0_5__quarantine_gate are excluded by name. Occurrences that existed on 2026-10-14 (about 50 across 10 docs/plan files, 11 imported tracker records, no commit message) go into a committed baseline with per-file and per-record counts that every run reports; any occurrence beyond the baseline fails. The baseline is a counted fallback owned by a follow-up bead created now.
- Each check has a negative fixture showing it rejects: infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency covers (a), (b) and (c) (adding calc-engine to dna-onecalc or calc-host to calc-fml, an OS import in a portable package, a native-only package without its wasm32 refusal). (d), (e) and (f) are proven by unit tests of the kind this package keeps, on fixtures under tools/xtask/tests/fixtures/, never by editing the real workspace.
- New dependencies only as the Do needs them, each named in the commit message (for example syn for (e)).

Rulings after round 1 (2026-10-14, orchestrator):
- Check (e) keeps the manifest half here; the coverage half (proving the named case reaches the caller, and refusing callers inside the defining library) is owned by dc-pz3u. seams.rs cites it and every receipt counts the seam entries whose reach is unproven.
- OS-binding deny list in (b) applies to the full wasm32-unknown-unknown closure of every portable package and to the direct dependencies of portable packages on every target; transitive host-target crates such as libc or rustix are allowed.
- (d) scans non-test, non-comment Rust code of portable packages including build.rs; tests/, benches/, examples/, #[cfg(test)] code and comments are out of its scope by design and the check's text says so. include!, include_str! and include_bytes! are not followed: (b) and (d) fail when a portable package uses one, until a bead extends them to follow it.

- The direct-dependency rule that dna-calc does not depend on calc-engine (plan section 1.3: skins never depend on engine internals; section 2.1: DNA Calc reaches the engine only through CalcHost) is confirmed; flagged for the owner's M0 review.
- The seams.json files created in every portable library package are part of this bootstrap, like infra-m0.1's acceptance.json files; from now on each bead edits only its own package's seams.json and acceptance.json.

title: Pin legacy sources and resolve inaccessible migration inputs
description:
## Outcome
Pin legacy sources and resolve inaccessible migration inputs. The behaviour is available through the Infrastructure production path described below, with the named acceptance cases passing.

## Context
Implements §§1, 10–13 of DNA_CALC_REIMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, within Bootstrap checkpoint — independent lanes, CI and evidence safety. Own only Infrastructure files for this task; consume prerequisite APIs rather than editing another library. Production route: cargo xtask / calcctl; call the same exported library entrypoints as the applications.

## Do
Record commit IDs, working-tree state and blob hashes for every legacy repository under the DnaCalc root (OxFunc, OxFml, OxCalc, OxDoc, DnaTreeCalc, the archived DnaOneCalc, OxReplay, OxXlPlay, ExcelFunctionsHandbook, DnaVisiCalc, Foundation) and the exact files/symbols selected by each port task. All of these are available locally; the 2026-10-12 review found uncommitted changes in OxCalc (consumer.rs and three grid/machine files), OxDoc (oxdoc-xlsx lib.rs plus an untracked cell-add conformance fixture), OxFml (eval/mod.rs) and DnaTreeCalc (.beads only): commit or stash them in those repositories first so every pinned blob is a committed object. Record parser, function-family, corpus and oracle-runner file lists before copying. Mark any module that is genuinely absent as unavailable and route its tasks to fresh implementation.
Add the named acceptance tests to this package's acceptance suite and register their exact names in its local acceptance manifest. Keep imported-source blob IDs and any changed semantic witnesses in the migration record. All proposed commands become real repository commands through infra-m0.3; a zero-test run is a failure.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.4 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.4 --platform linux --require-all
```
- `infra_m0_4__source_manifest`: Every selected port input has a repository, commit, path, content hash, license status and read disposition, and no pinned blob comes from an uncommitted working tree.
- `infra_m0_4__missing_source`: A port input absent from the pinned manifest is reported as unavailable and never counted as a verified reusable implementation.
The acceptance runner must verify every named case actually executed and retain the machine-readable receipt. Assertions compare observable outputs, operation effects or independently instrumented calls, not a success flag assigned by the implementation itself.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux for repository/tooling execution. Artifacts produced here are consumed by wasm/browser CI; this bead does not imply running a native CLI inside wasm.

## Out of scope
Other command/function families and performance tuning. Do not add a second evaluator, a tree reference language, platform-specific code to portable libraries, or a hidden fallback. Any missing prerequisite requires an explicit dependent bead, not a local substitute.
notes:
Provisional plan ID: infra-m0.4. Native export preserves this ID; acceptance command IDs and test names use the same stable plan identity.

Sharpened at claim (2026-10-14):
- State on 2026-10-14 (read-only check): all eleven repositories are clean with nothing to commit or stash first. OxFunc and OxFml each hold one stash (OxFml's stash@{0} is the fml-gpz exploration and is not a pin source). ExcelFunctionsHandbook's HEAD 30c5b03 is one commit ahead of origin. OxDoc has no license file. OxVba (C:\Work\DnaCalc\OxVba) is cited by three beads' Port from text although the Do's list omits it, so pin it too.
- The manifest is the migration record: migration/source-manifest.json, written only by `cargo xtask pin-sources` and later by Infrastructure disposition beads, never by hand. Per repository: name, origin URL, pinned commit (HEAD), whether that commit is on origin, working-tree state and stash count at pin time, and the license file name with its blob. Per port input: the citing bead IDs (taken from the Port from sections of .beads/issues.jsonl, which are authoritative), repository, path (a cited directory expands to its files), blob hash at the pinned commit, the symbols the Port from text names that the blob contains, a category (parser, function-family, corpus, oracle-runner, other), license status and read disposition. No timestamps other than one pin date, so regeneration is reproducible.
- Read dispositions: port (may be copied after review); reference (read for behaviour only: the Port from text says behavioural reference, ideas, precedent, lessons or discovery location); quarantined (OxFunc/crates/oxfunc_core/src/excel_numeric/x87.rs and the paths infra-m0.5 lists, pending that bead); unavailable (cited but absent at the pinned commit; report each with its beads so the orchestrator can route them to fresh implementation). License status is read from the repository's license file and recorded as found, or as none-found when there is no file; it is never inferred.
- Legacy repositories are read-only: use only read commands (rev-parse, ls-tree, cat-file, `branch -r --contains`, `--no-optional-locks status`). No fetch, checkout, stash or index write. `git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain` of every legacy repository is identical before and after, and the case records that.
- Legacy root: the workspace root's parent directory by default, overridden by DNACALC_LEGACY_ROOT, and recorded in the receipt. The Linux run in the WSL clone reads the Windows repositories through DNACALC_LEGACY_ROOT=/mnt/c/Work/DnaCalc, passing `-c safe.directory=<repo>` on each git call rather than changing any git config. A host where the legacy root is absent prints ACCEPT-NOT-RUN with that reason.
- Port beads look an input up with `cargo xtask pin-sources --lookup <Repo>/<path>`. It prints the pinned entry (commit, blob, disposition), or `unavailable` with a non-zero exit. infra_m0_4__missing_source uses this route, and the manifest's summary counts never put an unavailable or quarantined input among verified reusable ones.
- infra_m0_4__source_manifest re-derives every entry's blob with its own `git rev-parse <commit>:<path>` call, independently of the generator. It checks that each entry carries all six fields and each pinned commit exists as a commit object (so no blob comes from an uncommitted working tree), and that a fresh `pin-sources` run reproduces the committed manifest apart from the pin date.
- Not pinned: OxFunc/smart-fuzzer cache and runs (bulk evidence; infra-m0.6 and DnaCalc/OxFunc-Evidence). Pushing ExcelFunctionsHandbook is the owner's act: record `on_origin: false` and report it.
close_reason:
Product status: `cargo xtask pin-sources` pins twelve legacy repositories (the eleven named plus OxVba) at their HEADs in migration/source-manifest.json, read-only, and `cargo xtask pin-sources --lookup <Repo>/<path>` answers port beads (exit 0 pinned port or reference, 1 unavailable, 3 quarantined, 4 unpinned bulk evidence). 2210 inputs: 880 port, 412 reference, 911 quarantine_derived, 7 quarantined, 0 unavailable, 2 excluded; every input provisional (nothing compiled, dc-4r4l). Source-discovery paths are reference with 30 runner_candidate inputs handed to infra-m1.2 (noted there; a change from plan section 10.2 for the owner's review). Build commit 106ed72, pushed.
Evidence: Windows (rustc/cargo 1.94.1), accept-receipts/infra-m0.4/windows.json: "ACCEPT passed infra_m0_4__source_manifest (package xtask, exit code 0)", "ACCEPT passed infra_m0_4__missing_source (package xtask, exit code 0)", RESULT passed, 2 selected, 2 passed, architecture checks 6/6, exit code 0; transcripts target/accept/infra-m0.4/exit-codes.txt: pin-sources 0, lookups 0/1/3/4, cargo test -p xtask --bins 54 passed, fmt 0, clippy -D warnings 0; manifest byte-identical before and after the accept runs; HEAD and `git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain` of all twelve legacy repositories identical before, after the Windows pass and after the Linux run. Linux (WSL Ubuntu, rustc/cargo 1.93.1, clone at 106ed72, DNACALC_LEGACY_ROOT=/mnt/c/Work/DnaCalc), accept-receipts/infra-m0.4/linux.json: both cases passed, RESULT passed, architecture checks 6/6, exit code 0 (the fresh pin reproduced the committed manifest).
Still open: dc-xz2t (per-bead family and symbol selection, 38 unresolved family terms, disposition accuracy), dc-4r4l (compile audition), dc-1c6a (4 include_str!(concat!) skips and the w111 evidence files), dc-jtlu (case checks and lookup codes), infra-m0.5 (dispositions of quarantine_derived inputs, quarantined helpers and replay evidence).
